text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's government has had enough of the ethnic crisis in oil-producing Warri and will come out with drastic measures to restore order in the area, a member of the ruling military council says.
- Pipelines carrying fuel from the Warri oil refinery to a local depot have been vandalised, but the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation says this will not lead to fuel shortages.

- The naira on Friday depreciated on the street market to 89 to the dollar from 86 to the dollar. Foreign exchange dealers said there was no sign of an anticipated appreciation of the naira following the return of Moslem pilgrims from Saudi Arabia.
- The military government is putting together a decree that will specify guidelines for a programme that is designed to mobilise wealth through rural industrialisation.
- Closure of Ogidigben flow stations, near Warri, at the weekend has further hit oil production by Nigeria's Royal Dutch/Shell unit.
- Nigeria Airways is to resume flights immediately, after resolving an insurance payment problem which had kept planes grounded for a month.

- Industrialists and financial analysts say Nigeria's productivity has dropped, blaming the inability of the government to begin basic projects and policies promised in the budget. These projects include: payment of local debts, privatisation of some public agencies, transfer of the central bank's retail functions.
- Nigeria's rising profile in cashew nut exports may soon be bolstered by the arrival of buyers from India.
- Participants at an oil and gas forum have urged the government to share crude oil royalties directly with communities in oil-producing areas.
